newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador unions extend Wednesday strike to 48 hours.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador unions extend Wednesday strike to 48 hours.

text.p: The organisers of Ecuador's largest general strike in recent years said on Tuesday the stoppage scheduled for Wednesday would last for one more day.
"The Patriotic Front has decided to extend the general strike to 48 hours from 24 hours," Humberto Luzardo, president of the Confederation of Ecuadorean Workers, told Reuters.
A spokesman for indigenous groups said a million indigenous Ecuadorans had already blocked major roads across the country to protest against President Abdala Bucaram's economic austerity measures.
"From today we have taken the main roads of the country," Antonio Vargas, the president of the Confederation of Indigenous Nationalities of Ecuador, told Reuters.
He said the heaviest blockades were in the mountain regions of Canar, Chimborazo, Tungurahua, Pichnicha and Imbabura, where 600,000 protesters were taking part.
"The road blocks are planned to last until Friday but they may be extended for an indefinite period depending on the protesters," Vargas said.
Police were preparing an operation to reopen the roads, but Vargas said he had received no reports of clashes.
Truck drivers began an indefinite strike on Monday which has led to gasoline shortages. But students have been the most active protesters in recent weeks.
Discontent has grown in Ecuador after the six-month-old government introduced austerity measures that include price-hikes for electricity, telephone services and public transport.
Bucaram has launched ambitious economic reforms to cut government spending. One of his key policy aims is to peg the value of the local sucre currency to the U.S. dollar.
Bucaram's election was largely due to the vote of the country's indigenous peoples, who make up 40 percent of Ecuador's population of 11.7 million.
